project.title: Rapid granulation versus functional imbalance of aerobic granular sludge under F-53B and OBS stress: A ROS-mediated metabolic trade-off mechanism
project.description: As the main alternatives to perfluorooctane sulfonate, 6:2 chlorinated polyfluorinated ether sulfonate (F-53B) and sodium p-perfluorous nonenoxybenzene sulfonate (OBS) pose concerns regarding their long-term accumulation in wastewater treatment systems. However, their impact on the formation process of aerobic granular sludge (AGS) remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of F-53B and OBS on sludge performance and microbial community structure during AGS granulation through long-term exposure experiments. The results demonstrated that both F-53B and OBS induced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, leading to cell damage and consequently inhibiting AGS system performance. However, both compounds significantly accelerated sludge granulation by stimulating extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) secretion compared to control group. Multi-omics analysis revealed that excessive ROS activated signal transduction pathways (RpoS/c-di-GMP) and upregulated key genes involved in energy metabolism pathways (glycolysis and TCA cycle), thereby prompting EPS-producing bacteria (e.g., Candidatus_Competibacter) to synthesize more EPS as a protective barrier and accelerating granule aggregation. During this process, the microbial community redirected energy allocation from pollutant removal to EPS synthesis, leading to competitive inhibition of functional bacteria involved in nitrogen and phosphorus removal (e.g., Candidatus_Accumulibacter and Nitrosomonas), ultimately resulting in reduced system treatment efficiency. Enzyme activity assays and molecular docking simulations further demonstrated that F-53B exerted stronger inhibitory effects than OBS by forming more stable hydrogen bonds with key antioxidant enzymes (SOD and CAT), thereby exacerbating ROS accumulation and subsequent EPS secretion. These findings provide a scientific basis for assessing the ecological risks of perfluoroalkyl substance alternatives and optimizing the stability of AGS processes.
